name: Lesson 6 · Counting: numbers 0–20, prices and age

cards.note: Numbers 0–20. Counting, one is eins; before a noun it becomes the article ein.
Numbers 0–20. zwei. On the phone Germans often say zwo, so it is not mixed up with drei.
Numbers 0–20. For age, sein and the number are enough: ist drei.
Numbers 0–20. Euro takes no plural ending after a number: zwei Euro.
Numbers 0–20. vier: the ie is a long i, as in English see.
Numbers 0–20. fünf, with ü.
Numbers 0–20. sechs: the chs sounds like ks.
Numbers 0–20. sieben has two syllables: sie-ben.
Numbers 0–20. acht, with the ch from the back of the throat.
Numbers 0–20. neun: eu sounds like oy in boy.
Numbers 0–20. zehn: the z sounds like ts, the h is silent.
Numbers 0–20. elf is a word of its own, like English eleven.

cards.front: How old is the dog? – He is **twelve**.
cards.back: Wie alt ist der Hund? – Er ist **zwölf**.
cards.note: Numbers 0–20. zwölf, like elf, is not built from zehn.
Numbers 0–20. From 13, the unit comes first, then zehn: drei-zehn, like thir-teen.
Numbers 0–20. vier + zehn, written as one word.
Numbers 0–20. fünf + zehn: fünfzehn.
Numbers 0–20. sechzehn drops the s of sechs: not sechszehn.
Numbers 0–20. siebzehn drops the -en of sieben: not siebenzehn.
Numbers 0–20. acht + zehn, nothing dropped.

cards.front: How old are you? (one friend) – I am **nineteen**.
cards.back: Wie alt bist du? – Ich bin **neunzehn**.
cards.note: Numbers 0–20. neun + zehn: neunzehn.
Numbers 0–20. zwanzig: the tens end in -zig, and zwei shortens to zwan-.
Numbers 0–20. zwanzig Euro: Euro stays the same after any number.
Numbers 0–20. null before a noun is a casual way of saying none at all, as with English zero.
Numbers 0–20. null: zero. Counting starts with null, eins.

cards.front: Is the cat ten? – No, she is **eleven**.
cards.back: Ist die Katze zehn? – Nein, sie ist **elf**.
cards.note: Numbers 0–20. A question with the verb first gets ja or nein; elf is eleven.
Numbers 0–20. sieben, acht: seven, eight.

cards.front: What does the bread cost? – **Three** euros.
cards.note: Numbers 0–20. drei Euro: the number, then Euro without a plural ending.

cards.front: Does the coffee cost **two** or three euros?
cards.back: Kostet der Kaffee **zwei** oder drei Euro?
cards.note: Numbers 0–20. A yes/no question with the verb first; zwei Euro.
Numbers 0–20. Before a noun one is the article ein, and kostet takes the accusative: einen Euro.
Numbers 0–20. der Euro, so einen Euro, whatever the thing that costs it.
Numbers 0–20. Ages work the same for everyone: sein + the number.

cards.front: Why does the tea cost **twenty** euros?
cards.note: Numbers 0–20. Question word first, then kostet, then the subject.
